cards.text: Friend, the Teacher, son of David and king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1), has spent a while watching people chase the wind (Ecclesiastes 4:16). Now he turns to the house of God and says to guard your steps when you go there. Think of the new hire on day one, watching every single step.

He warns about something he calls the sacrifice of fools, offered by people who do not know that they do wrong. That's me, friend, humming proudly by the oven for a whole HOUR before I noticed it was never turned ON.

cards.question: At the house of God, the Teacher says to draw near to ___ rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools.

cards.text: Next he goes after the mouth: don't be quick to speak, don't be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God, and let your words be few. You know when somebody fires off a reply in the group chat before they finish READING it? FIVE replies deep in the WRONG conversation.

cards.question: The reason the Teacher gives for letting your words be few before God is that God is in heaven and you are on earth.

cards.text: Then he paints a picture: as a dream comes through many cares. You know the one, friend, that stressed-out week when you dream your boss is a goose running the Monday meeting.

cards.question: In the Teacher's picture, a dream comes through many cares. Whose speech does he say comes with many words?

cards.text: Now the Teacher turns to vows made to God. I promised my oven a clean rack back in March, friend, and that oven has NOT forgotten.

cards.question: The Teacher says that once you make a vow to God, you can take your time fulfilling it.
God takes no pleasure in fools, the Teacher says, so fulfill your vow. What does he say is better than making a vow to God and not fulfilling it?

answers.text: Not making a vow at all
Letting a priest vow for you

cards.text: Then the Teacher warns: don't let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and don't try to talk your way out of a vow with the messenger. My mouth once bragged I could carry SIX trays at once, friend, and it was NOT my mouth that landed face-down in the chocolate chips.

cards.question: The Teacher says not to tell the messenger that your vow was a ___.
The Teacher asks why God should be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands.

cards.text: He comes back to the dream picture: as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. I once talked to a bowl of dough for TEN minutes about how great it was gonna be, friend. Still dough.

cards.question: After all those warnings about words and vows, what does the Teacher tell us to do?
